problem: Latency- and trust-aware topology selection can still choose a fleet that exceeds the RAM, vCPU, or Qube budget available on the target machine.

independentReviews.preferredApproach: fail-closed resource budgets evaluated after trust/readiness gates
independentReviews.reason: A topology is not deployable merely because its DAG timing is correct; resource feasibility must be an explicit qualification invariant.

independentReviews.preferredApproach: retain forbidden capability co-residency constraints before resource ranking
independentReviews.reason: A cheaper topology must never win by violating an isolation boundary. Security constraints remain authoritative over resource savings.
It adds no qrexec calls, workers, daemons, or production state while exposing the Qube/RAM/vCPU tradeoff before VM deployment.

approachesCompared.name: latency-and-trust-only topology ranking
approachesCompared.failure: Can select a correct fast layout that the host cannot afford in RAM/vCPU/Qube count.

approachesCompared.name: measure resources only in live Qubes
approachesCompared.failure: Higher fidelity but too late and environment-dependent for first-pass topology elimination.

approachesCompared.name: deterministic worker resource profiles plus hard budgets
approachesCompared.whyItWon: Preserves correctness and trust gates, adds explicit RAM/vCPU/Qube feasibility, costs only local linear validation, and does not change MissionQueue/coordinator semantics.

qa: two-worker balanced topology wins under a 3-Qube/3072MB/4-vCPU budget while preserving 210ms-equivalent critical path
one-worker topology remains resource-cheap but fails latency readiness
four-worker isolated topology remains timing-correct but fails the tighter resource budget
forbidden coder+QA co-residency rejects the fused two-worker topology before resource ranking
expanded budget permits the isolated four-worker topology to win when the trust boundary requires it
missing or invalid resource profiles fail closed
lessons: Worker-count minimization alone is not a sufficient proxy for memory or CPU pressure.
Resource optimization must remain subordinate to trust-boundary and correctness gates.
Synthetic resource profiles are planning evidence, not a substitute for measured Qubes RSS/CPU during real qualification.
nextGate: Calibrate worker RAM/vCPU profiles from synthetic Qubes measurements, then feed the measured profile into the same evaluator before real-worker qualification.
